articles.title: Targeted Atopic Dermatitis Therapies Cut Hospitalizations But Raise Pharmacy Costs
articles.summary: Targeted therapies for atopic dermatitis effectively reduce emergency room visits and hospitalizations, but drive up specialty drug spending for commercial plans. Self-funded employers must balance these higher upfront pharmacy benefit costs against potential medical cost offsets.
articles.source_line: Source: Managed Healthcare Executive; Sun, 01 Nov 2026 22:02:25 GMT

articles.title: Andel and Novo Offer GLP-1 Coverage Workarounds for Employers
articles.summary: As self-funded employers increasingly restrict GLP-1 coverage due to unsustainable costs, manufacturers and health innovators are introducing alternative access models and workarounds. This development directly impacts how employer health plans manage skyrocketing specialty drug spend and design obesity benefits.
articles.source_line: Source: The American Journal of Managed Care® (AJMC®); Nov 1, 2026
articles.source_name: The American Journal of Managed Care® (AJMC®)

articles.title: Republican Lawmakers Lead Antitrust Scrutiny Against CVS and Major PBMs
articles.summary: Bipartisan and increasingly Republican-led antitrust investigations are targeting major pharmacy benefit managers like CVS, signaling mounting legislative pressure on PBM business models. This political shift highlights growing momentum for federal PBM reform, which could significantly impact pricing transparency and contract structures for self-funded employers.

articles.title: RAND and USC Research Shows Self-Insured Employers Struggle to Control Costs
articles.summary: Recent research from RAND and USC reveals that even large self-insured employers are struggling to effectively rein in escalating healthcare costs. This highlights the ongoing challenge self-funded plan sponsors face and reinforces the critical need for advanced cost-management strategies and PBM optimization.

articles.title: Zepbound Sales Surge 49% Amid Volume Growth and Lower Net Prices
articles.summary: Eli Lilly reported a 49% increase in Zepbound sales to $5.35 billion driven by higher volume despite lower net prices. This trend highlights the intensifying financial impact of GLP-1 medications on commercial health plans, requiring self-funded employers to closely manage utilization and formulary strategies.
articles.source_line: Source: Medical Daily; Sun, 01 Nov 2026 16:46:32 GMT
